source.title: Challenges of Symbolic Computation: My Favorite Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Given a polynomial f(x, y) with rational coefficients and a rational error tolerance ε, decide in time polynomial in the degree and coefficient size whether there exists a polynomial f̂(x, y) over the complex numbers that factors nontrivially over C[x, y] and lies within distance ε of f for a reasonable norm on the coefficient vector.

evidence.quote:

accepted.question_text: Let A be a black-box n × n matrix over an abstract field, where the representation of A is a routine for matrix-vector multiplication. Under the target resource bounds of O(n) black-box calls, n^2(log n)^{O(1)} arithmetic operations in the field, and O(n) intermediate field elements of storage, compute the characteristic polynomial of A; randomized algorithms, including Monte Carlo algorithms, are allowed.

accepted.question_text: Devise a public-key cryptosystem based on diophantine linear algebra whose security is not broken by lattice basis reduction algorithms.

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 4
Devise a public key cryptosystem that is based on diophantine linear algebra but that
is safe from lattice basis reduction.

An alter￾native cryptosystem is described in (Ajtai and Dwork, 1997, Goldreich et al., 1997a)
and proven secure provided that computing a short non-zero lattice vector is hard.

accepted.question_text: Develop methods for computing Gröbner bases approximately by iterative system-solving techniques such as Gauss-Seidel, conjugate gradient, Newton, or related iterative methods, in a way that can plug into numerical software, compute some bases faster than exact arithmetic, and still recover structural information such as the basis structure, for example by using modular arithmetic.

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 5
Compute Grobner bases approximately by iterative methods for solving ¨ systems, such
as Gauss-Seidel, conjugate gradient, Newton,...
A solution plugs into numerical software and computes some bases faster than by ex￾act arithmetic; the structure of the bases may be determined, e.g., by modular arith￾metic.

accepted.question_text: Suppose one is given an algorithm that computes A·y for inputs A ∈ K^(m×n) and y ∈ K^n using T(m,n) field operations and S(m,n) auxiliary space. Construct, in a way applicable to practical problems, an algorithm for the transposed product A^T·z with z ∈ K^m that uses O(T(m,n)) time while simultaneously using O(S(m,n)) space.

evidence.quote: Here is then our sixth open problem.

Open Problem 6
With inputs A ∈ Km×n and y ∈ Kn
you are given an algorithm for A · y that uses

T(m,n) arithmetic field operations and S(m,n) auxiliary space. Show how to con￾struct an algorithm for AT
·z where z ∈ Km that uses O(T(m,n)) time and simultane￾ously O(S(m,n)) space. Your construction must be applicable to practical problems.

accepted.question_text: Devise a plug-and-play and generic-programming methodology for symbolic mathematical computation that is widely adopted by algorithm designers, commercial symbolic-software producers, and outside users, so that symbolic software components can be assembled and reused across systems in practice.

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 7
Devise a plug-and-play and generic programming methodology for symbolic math￾ematical computation that is widely adopted by the experts in algorithm design, the
commercial symbolic software producers, and the outsider users.

However, our symbolic software is becoming very complex and a
solution to Problem 7 is crucial.

accepted.question_text: Find, besides mathematics education, another application area for symbolic computation that functions as a true 'killer application'—that is, an application whose demand makes the software written for it a commercial success.

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 8
Besides mathematics education, find another so-called "killer" application for sym￾bolic computation.

The problem is solved when the new application makes the software written for it a
commercial success.

accepted.question_text: Modify the Risch integration algorithm, or replace it with another algorithm, so that it produces antiderivatives that are continuous on domains of maximum extent; alternatively, give a clear description of the largest class of functions, elementary or otherwise, for which continuous antidifferentiation can be performed efficiently. A satisfactory solution should come with a correctness proof published in a strong journal, or preferably with an implementation in a major computer algebra system that makes the method available for broad use and scrutiny.

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 9
Modify (or replace) the Risch algorithm so as to produce integrals continuous on
domains of maximum extent, or else clearly describe the largest class of functions
(elementary or other) for which continuous antidifferentiation can be done efficiently.

This problem will be known to be solved when a proof of the algorithm’s correct￾ness appears in a good journal, or more preferably when the algorithm is implemented
in a major CAS and thus made available for general use and scrutiny.
